title: Host-scheduled GQA prefill with HiFloat8 Q and K
formula: out = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128)) @ V over one shared KV head, computed as score^T = K @ Q^T; HiFloat8 Q[M,128] and K[N,128] in uint8 carriers, BF16 V[N,128] and out[M,128], FP32 online state merged across host-owned key intervals
study_for: The two drains out of L0C split along DIFFERENT axes, and the code says why: grep `SPLITN` in kernel.py. The score tile is computed transposed (`score^T = K @ Q^T`), so the query rows are its N axis and `SPLITN` is what hands each vector sub-block 64 of them. The PV drain a page later is the bare `ub_pv[d2] <<= l0c_pv[d2]`, SPLITM by default, because there the query rows are the M axis. "Always SPLITM" is the wrong generalisation; "split whichever axis carries the query rows" is the rule.
The same comment carries the cost of the alternative on this shape: an fp32 -> fp32 dual destination is a cheap fixpipe, and the fp16 SINGLE-mode path it replaced measured +82us.

A forward-only L1 ring for the P tile: grep `vec_ready` and `wait_vec` -- raw flags on MTE3/MTE1 with no backward edge, which the comment marks as intra-block rather than S/FFTS. A mutex would have added a return edge this handoff does not need.

Flash-decoding partials reach the workspace only at an m-block boundary, into a head or tail slot chosen by which end of the key range this core owns: grep `fd_accum`, `head_ws`, `tail_ws`. The slot numbers are not computed on the device -- they arrive in fa_meta, which `reference.schedule` builds.

`schedule` offers four core splits and the four declared cases select only three of them: `staggered`, `whole_query` and `even`. The fourth, `fia`, is a recorded 28-core cost-aware split taken from a real run, and it is live code on a live branch — it simply has no case. Read it against the three that do run, and add a case with "schedule": "fia" if you want to exercise it; nothing else has to change.
do_not_copy_when: Your score tile is not transposed. The SPLITN drain, the `.T` on both PV operands and the 2-key pack demux into `l1p` are all consequences of `K @ Q^T`; take one without the others and the query rows land in the wrong sub-block.

More than two cores can own one query tile. The metadata ABI and the head/tail workspace slots assume at most two active core intervals intersect a tile, and `build_metadata` refuses a three-way split rather than encoding it.

You want to change block_dim without rebuilding the metadata. fa_meta carries exactly one row per launched core and fd_meta two, so the launch width is part of the input, not a tuning parameter -- the launched cores beyond `work_cores` are emitted disabled precisely so they still reach the vector-wide barrier.
